So it really would fail, including for an added optional field, rather than silently returning null.

handoff.compile_time_link: _hostShapeLinked (ask-answers.ts:33) is a type-level identity between z.infer of the runtime parser hostDetails and the host's AskToolDetails. A host shape change, including an added optional field or a nested field, makes tsc report 'Type true is not assignable to type false' on that line; the parse itself also fails at runtime for changed required fields, so the parser cannot silently return null for a known shape.
risks: Password-type form fields appear unmasked in turn-judge timeline and {{ask_answers}}: the host writes raw values into details.answers, and the module cannot see field types. Fixing it needs the host to mark secret fields in AskToolDetails; a separate item.

The identity-type trick depends on zod's inferred object type identity; a future zod upgrade that changes inference could fail the link without a host change (would show as a tsc error on line 33, not silently).
